source_status.exact_result: Unverified author proof: for every good separated strict boundaryless pure n-dimensional K-analytic space (n >= 1), including singular and nonreduced structures, and every continuous finite h, the ordinary zero-Hessian current equation is equivalent before and after a quadratic Galois extension E/K admitting a unit a with |a-sigma(a)|=1. The equivalence iterates through finite towers of such quadratic stages. The proof supplies exact local invariant polynomial-superform descent and fixed-support C2 upstairs approximation of invariant compact ordinary forms.
concrete_gaps: Original P06.2 classical pluriharmonic recognition and two-sign regularization remain unproved.
Quadratic extensions lacking the residue-separating unit condition and general finite Galois or separable extensions outside the stated finite towers remain unproved.
Completion of infinite algebraic extensions, transcendental analytic extensions and the universal classical curve-test bridge remain separate obligations.
Exact descent of arbitrary invariant ordinary smooth forms is not claimed; controlled differentiated approximation suffices for the proved current equation.
The draft has an author self-audit but no independent verification verdict.

source_clarification.before: CLD Corollary 15.2.9 states: if $X$ is locally holomorphically separated, $F\subset X$ is closed and countable at infinity (in particular compact), and $U_i$ is an ordinary open cover of $F$, there are nonnegative ordinary smooth $\theta_i$, each compactly supported inside $U_i$, locally finite, with $\sum_i\theta_i=1$ near $F$. Only finite covers of compact sets are used.
source_clarification.after: For a compact subset $F$ and a finite ordinary open cover $(U_i)$ of $F$, there are nonnegative ordinary smooth $\theta_i$, each compactly supported inside $U_i$, with $\sum_i\theta_i=1$ near $F$. This compact specialization follows from CLD Corollary 15.2.5 and ordinary smooth functional calculus. For each $x\in F$, apply 15.2.5 with $\{x\}\subset U_i$ to obtain a smooth function equal to one near $x$ and compactly supported in $U_i$. Compose with a nonnegative smooth real function equal to zero near zero and equal to one near one, obtaining a nonnegative bump with the same support containment. Compactness selects finitely many such bumps; group them by cover index into $\psi_i$, and put $s=\sum_i\psi_i$. Then $s>0$ near $F$. Apply 15.2.5 again to compact $F$ inside the open $\{s>0\}$, and the same nonnegative composition, to obtain $\chi$ compactly supported there and equal to one near $F$. Set $\theta_i=\chi\psi_i/s$ on that open and extend by zero. Smoothness follows since the support of $\chi$ lies compactly inside the open. Each $\theta_i$ has compact support inside $U_i$ and their sum is $\chi$. No arbitrary countable-at-infinity, fixed-cover-index compact-support assertion is used. Only this compact-set, finite-cover version is needed.
source_clarification.reason: Source-citation compact specialization; no theorem or actual use changed
